newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Kohl wraps up Brazil visit pledging closer ties.
newsitem.headline: Kohl wraps up Brazil visit pledging closer ties.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Wednesday wrapped up an action-packed 24-hour visit to Brazil, pledging to inject a shot of adrenalin into economic and political ties.

Kohl, on a three-nation Latin American tour with a pack of high-powered German businessmen in tow, said investment in Brazil's privatisation programme and closer cooperation on technical and environmental issues would top the agenda.
"Brazil will be one of the great nations of the future in the next century," Kohl told reporters.
He said he agreed with Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in talks on Tuesday they would both give the highest priority to giving relations a "new boost, a new dynamism, a new quality."
The German leader pledged he and Cardoso would personally oversee the development of bilateral ties through regular telephone calls in the future.
The businessmen travelling with the chancellor on a tour that began in Argentina and was scheduled to end in Mexico also vowed to intensify their interests in Latin America's largest country.

No new investments were announced, but Christian Roth, head of the German builders group Hauptverband der Deutschen Bauindustrie, told Reuters they would be returning to Germany with the message that "Brazil is a country to invest in."

Germany is the second-largest foreign investor in Brazil, sporting a portfolio amounting to $7 billion in 1995. It is also Brazil's third-most important trading partner, with more than $7 billion a year in bilateral trade.
Ties between Europe's economic powerhouse and Latin America's largest economy have been traditionally close.

Relations began with German immigration at the beginning of the 19th century. A wane in ties during and after the Second World War, when Brazil joined the Allies to fight the Nazis, was followed by a flood of investments during the 1960s and 1970s.
After that German firms became major players in Brazil. There are 1,200 German companies in Sao Paulo alone.
The business delegation accompanying Kohl included Ferdinand Piech of car giant Volkswagen AG and Heinrich von Pierer of electronics firm Siemens AG.
